summary: Mount Keith Airport is a remote mining airfield in Western Australia's Goldfields region, primarily serving the Mount Keith nickel mine operated by BHP. The airport supports FIFO (fly-in fly-out) workers commuting to the mine site, with regular charter flights from Perth. Its remote location in the arid outback makes it one of the more isolated operational airfields in the region.
faqs:
Q: Where is Mount Keith Airport located?
A: The airport is situated in the Northern Goldfields region of Western Australia, approximately 400 km north of Kalgoorlie and around 850 km northeast of Perth.

Q: Who uses Mount Keith Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves mining personnel working at the Mount Keith nickel operation, with charter and FIFO flights being the main source of traffic.

Q: Are there commercial passenger flights to Mount Keith?
A: No scheduled commercial services operate to the airport. Access is typically arranged through employer-organized charter flights for mining staff.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport has minimal passenger facilities, as it is primarily a work site airstrip. Travelers should expect basic amenities only.
transport_tips: There is no public transport to or from Mount Keith Airport, so ground transport must be pre-arranged, typically through the employing mining company. Most visitors fly in on company-chartered aircraft from Perth and are shuttled directly to the mine site. Private vehicle access is via unsealed roads, and fuel and supplies should be carried before departing from the nearest town.
local_tip: Temperatures at Mount Keith can swing dramatically between scorching daytime heat and surprisingly cold nights, so even in summer bring a warm layer if you're arriving after dark.
